key_insight: A hybrid MILP–QUBO framework preserves routing feasibility while enabling modest distance savings, but current QAOA hardware is reliable only for very small subproblems.
engineering_relevance: Vehicle-level decomposition offers a practical way to integrate optimization backends into constrained fleet routing without a monolithic QUBO.
method: Combine classical MILP with vehicle-level QUBO subproblems.
Solve QUBOs using Toshiba SQBM+ and QAOA on Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Emerald.
Validate feasibility and accept only improvements over classical baselines.
evidence_signal: Across five London-derived benchmarks with 10–70 customers, SQBM+ reduced fleet distance by 2.80% and 0.22% on the 25- and 55-customer instances; reliable QAOA constraint satisfaction was limited to subproblems of up to 4 customers (16 qubits).
watch_item: The reported distance gains come from SQBM+, not evidence of quantum advantage; assignment-level time-window tightness remains the dominant scalability bottleneck.
paper_title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Optimization for CVRPTW: A Systems Framework with Provable Feasibility and Empirical Hardware Limits
